Hi Samir / Leah —

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion and clear decision criteria around latency, data residency, and cost predictability. Quick recap from our side and a suggested legal/ procurement sequence so we can keep momentum:

1) Discovery highlights
- Primary use case: model-assisted credit-risk scoring for retail portfolio (inference-only; no model training on Greenline data).
- Decision criteria: 99th %-tile tail latency, deterministic per-token unit economics, and SOC2 + DPA controls.
- Timeline: target pilot start in early Oct (internal signoffs by mid-September).

2) Stakeholders (as we heard today — please flag corrections)
- Economic buyer: TBD (you flagged finance involvement)
- Product / technical owner: Samir Shah (you)
- Procurement lead: Leah Ortiz (you)
- Security / vendor risk: you said security team would be engaged — need a primary contact

3) Proposed contract sequencing (to minimize friction)
- NDA (to be signed first; protects attachments/benchmarks)
- Security questionnaire / vendor risk assessment (send in parallel to NDA execution)
- MSA redline then DPA (MSA negotiation after security questions; DPA aligned to final MSA)
- PO / commercial order (can be issued once MSA + DPA are agreed or in parallel with a signed short-form commercial addendum)

4) Asks / next steps
- Samir / Leah: please confirm economic buyer and legal owner (name + email). If you prefer, we can start NDA via DocuSign and run the security questionnaire through your portal.
- I attached a one-page NDA template to speed signatures.

Subject: Legal sequencing + redline playbook (short note)

Samir / Leah —

Short note from legal/commerce side to set expectations on sequencing and typical turn times. Happy to hop on a call to walk through specifics.

1) NDA first — simple mutual NDA via DocuSign; target 1–3 business days. That gets confidentiality in place for attachments / benchmark material.
2) Security questionnaire — please route the questionnaire to our Security team (sec-answers@redwoodinference.com). We aim to return vendor risk assessments in 5 business days for standard questions, 7–10 days for SOC2 evidence requests.
3) MSA redline strategy:
   - We prefer a single MSA with commercial addendum. For faster procurement, we can sign a short-form commercial addendum that contains SOW, pricing, and PO terms while MSA redlines are in flight.
   - Typical negotiated MSA cycle: 7–14 business days if collaboration is tight; expect longer if there are custom indemnity or data residency terms.
4) DPA — aligned to MSA; if you require vendor-managed keys / HSM, flag early (that adds time).

Attachments: [Attachment: MSA_redline_guidance.docx (DOCX)]

Fallbacks / acceleration levers:
- Conditional PO tied to a signed short-form addendum (legal approval for revenue recognition teams).
- Executive approval path: if timeline is critical, we can surface the ask to our CRO and your CFO for an expedited SLA exception.

If Jordan or Maya want to see a redline exemplar before committing, I can provide a sanitized sample MSA redline (no commercial numbers) — tell me which clauses are priorities (indemnity, liability cap, data residency).

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
